last_action: JUNIPER IS DEPLOYED, INSTALLED AND IN USE. Live at juniper-navy.vercel.app since 2026-11-11, / is the deck and /grid is the grid, on the home screen as a standalone app. Six rounds of check-it-on-the-phone-and-fix-what-it-showed. (1) BACKUP IS NOW REACHABLE FROM THE DECK. Export and import were in the grid app's footer, unreachable once installed because standalone has no address bar — the only route to the only copy of a garden. The wordmark opens a Backup sheet: save, restore, start over. It SHARES rather than downloads, because in standalone WKWebView the `download` attribute is not dependable, and it builds the file when the sheet OPENS, because navigator.share must be called while the tap is still the current user activation. Confirmed working on the user's iPhone. (2) THE TITLE TYPE-SNAP IS GONE, and it was never the animation: the tile had a second set of sizes, and scale:true holds a card at its final layout size and scales it, so the title drew at the tile's 15px x 2.08 against the 30px it had a frame earlier. The face is now sized in cqw off the card's own width — name, rank, species, padding and band all measure a 0.0% step. Calibrated to the LAYOUT width (300px); the fan's rotation inflates the bounding rect to 313.3 and cost one wrong pass. container-type sits on .card__face, not .card, because it implies contain:layout which forces transform-style:flat and would collapse the 3D turn. (3) THE KEYBOARD SHORTCUTS WERE EATING TYPED TEXT — bound on the window with preventDefault regardless of focus, so a plant name could hold no space, no 'g' and no 'w'. Unnoticed because the demo garden filled those fields in. (4) THE REPO IS ONE APP. juniper-app/ and juniper-website/ removed with the root vercel.json and the Maestro workflow; CI and RUN_TEST.sh repointed at juniper-web, which had no CI at all. That is also what cleared the dependency alerts: 38 of 43 were the native build chain. The other five were juniper-web's dev dependencies (vite 6.4.6, vitest 5.1.0, two majors, no config change). npm audit now reports none.
next_action: (1) SAVE A BACKUP WITH REAL PLANTS IN IT. The garden has exactly one copy until this happens; the sheet's 'last backup' line exists to make the gap visible. (2) LIVE WITH IT. Everything structural is done and the remaining questions are not answerable by building: whether a fanned deck is the right way to meet your plants each morning, whether the dryness ramp reads at a glance, and whether use happens at all without a reminder (the D13 bet). (3) Decide on a service worker — the manifest alone got it on the home screen and earned the WebKit eviction exemption, but the app still needs the network on first paint each session. (4) Writing, not just reading: the per-plant journal renders but cannot be added to. (5) GitHub Actions billing still unverified since 2026-08-30, so CI cannot be trusted green or red — the workflow now at least points at the right app.

blockers.description: The garden still has exactly one copy. Backup and restore are now reachable from the installed app and the home-screen install exempts the origin from WebKit's seven-day eviction, but neither counts until a backup is actually saved somewhere that is not the phone.

Juniper is unvalidated by real use. The deck has been exercised hard but against a demo garden over two days. Whether a fanned deck is the right way to meet eight plants every morning, and whether the ramp reads at a glance, are questions only real plants over real weeks answer.
Juniper has no reminders at all. A deliberate bet (D13) that the deck is itself the reminder, and the only thing that settles it is whether use happens anyway.

There is no service worker, so the installed app needs the network on first paint of each session. The manifest alone was enough for the home screen and the eviction exemption; offline is a separate, unmade decision.
GitHub Actions billing unverified since 2026-08-30, so CI cannot be trusted green or red. The workflow itself now points at juniper-web, which it did not before 2026-11-12.
